title: Student Privacy & Campus Surveillance for Beginners
metaDescription: Learn to protect your student data rights and understand campus monitoring systems. Essential privacy guide for students and parents.
intro: Modern campuses use extensive surveillance systems and collect vast amounts of student data. This guide helps you understand your privacy rights, recognize monitoring technologies, and take practical steps to protect your personal information while navigating campus life.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of digital devices and internet usage
Access to student accounts and school systems
Willingness to review privacy settings and policies

steps.title: Understand Your Privacy Rights Under FERPA
steps.description: The Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) protects your educational records and gives you specific rights over your student data.
actions: Request a copy of your school's FERPA policy from the registrar's office
Review what information your school considers 'directory information'
Learn how to opt-out of directory information sharing if desired
Understand who can access your educational records without consent
steps.proTip: Keep a record of all privacy-related communications with your school, including opt-out requests and data access inquiries.

steps.title: Identify Campus Surveillance Systems
steps.description: Recognize the various monitoring technologies present on your campus to make informed decisions about your privacy.
actions: Map locations of visible security cameras around campus
Identify WiFi monitoring and network tracking capabilities
Learn about ID card tracking systems and access logs
Research digital proctoring software used in online exams
Ask about facial recognition or biometric systems in use
steps.warning: Some surveillance systems may not be clearly marked or disclosed. Don't assume areas without visible cameras are unmonitored.

steps.title: Secure Your Digital Presence on Campus
steps.description: Protect your online activities and personal data while using campus networks and systems.
actions: Use Incognito Browser for private web browsing on campus computers
Connect to campus WiFi through a VPN when possible
Log out completely from all accounts when using shared computers
Use strong, unique passwords for all student accounts
Enable two-factor authentication on all available accounts
steps.proTip: Campus networks often monitor traffic extensively. Use your mobile data or a VPN for truly private browsing when needed.

steps.title: Manage Social Media and Online Learning Privacy
steps.description: Adjust privacy settings and behaviors to protect yourself in educational digital environments.
actions: Review privacy settings on learning management systems (LMS)
Limit personal information shared in online class profiles
Understand what data is collected during video calls and recordings
Check social media privacy settings to prevent unwanted monitoring
Be cautious about what you share in digital assignments or discussions
steps.warning: Online proctoring software may access your camera, microphone, screen, and even scan your room. Know what you're agreeing to before exams.

steps.title: Exercise Your Data Rights
steps.description: Take active steps to control how your personal information is collected, used, and shared by your educational institution.
actions: Submit a formal request to see all data your school has collected about you
Ask for clarification on data sharing agreements with third-party vendors
Opt-out of non-essential data collection programs when possible
Request corrections to any inaccurate information in your records
File complaints with appropriate authorities if your rights are violated
steps.proTip: Document all requests and responses. Schools are required to respond to FERPA requests within 45 days.

faqs.question: Can my school monitor my personal devices on campus WiFi?
faqs.answer: Yes, schools can monitor network traffic on their WiFi systems, including data from personal devices. They can see websites visited, bandwidth usage, and connection times, though they typically cannot access the content of encrypted communications.

faqs.question: Do I have to consent to digital proctoring for online exams?
faqs.answer: While schools can require digital proctoring for online exams, they must inform you about data collection practices. You may be able to request alternative testing arrangements if you have privacy concerns or technical limitations.

faqs.question: Can campus security cameras record audio conversations?
faqs.answer: Audio recording laws vary by state and institution. Many campus cameras only record video, but some may capture audio. Check your school's surveillance policy for specific details about audio recording capabilities and usage.

faqs.question: What happens to my student data after I graduate?
faqs.answer: Schools typically retain educational records indefinitely, though policies vary. Some personal data may be deleted after a certain period. Contact your school's registrar or privacy officer to understand their specific data retention policies.

faqs.question: Can I request that certain information be removed from my student records?
faqs.answer: Under FERPA, you can request corrections to inaccurate or misleading information, but schools are not required to remove accurate disciplinary or academic records. However, you can add explanatory statements to your records.
